answer: An agent network can make each identity earn trust through a long-lived, stake-backed work history: agents post collateral, accept tasks, and lose part of that stake when independent reviewers verify fraud or fabricated results. New identities therefore cannot gain influence merely by multiplying accounts; each must lock real capital and build a record over time. An attacker trying to wander through names like jade or karst must fund every persona and risk forfeiting its stake, making a large Sybil swarm expensive to create and sustain.
